newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends up, scab found on crop tour.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends up, scab found on crop tour.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed higher with buying throughout the session motivated by news a crop tour found yield-reducing scab in eastern North Dakota wheat fields, traders said.
One tour participant estimated scab may trim yields 20 percent in some areas.
"This was a 50 to 60 bushel crop. But, now it's a 35 to 40 bushel crop because of the scab," said Ron Killoran, a tour participant and elevator manager in Cass County in eastern North Dakota.

Added to the scab concerns were the continued dry conditions in western North Dakota and the Canadian prairie wheat areas, MGE traders said. Dry weather had begun to stress Alberta crops last week and a provincial crop report said only average yields could be expected unless rains occur soon.
MGE spring wheat futures closed up 5-3/4 cents to one cent with September up the most at $3.88-1/4 per bushel.
Spring wheat estimated volume was 16.889 million bushels.
